chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The owner of the animal, the buyer, has the option (of keeping or returning) for three days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the buyer's option period when purchasing an animal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) specifies a three-day period for the buyer to inspect and decide on the quality of purchased animals, a ruling distinct from the general 'khiyar al-majlis' which typically ends upon parting of the meeting place. In Shia jurisprudence, this specific narration highlights the importance of consumer protection and the right of inspection (khiyar al-ayb) in commercial transactions, ensuring fairness in trade as practiced by the Ahl al-Bayt.
